full_narrative: Student SLIIT_02946: Psychosocial Risk Index is MODERATE (60.1/100). The primary contributing indicators elevating psychosocial risk are low or diminished peer social and academic support networks (score: 1.3) and elevated levels of academic stress (score: 4.3). This profile is actively buffered by moderate intrinsic academic motivation (score: 3.7), strong academic self-efficacy and belief in capability (score: 4.0), and moderate sense of campus belongingness (score: 3.0). Note that these psychosocial factors serve as contributing indicators to support proactive retention, rather than deterministic causes.
recommendations: Offer time-management workshops, workload review, or academic counseling check-in.
Connect student with peer study cohorts or collaborative lab partner pairings.
disclaimer: RESEARCH NOTICE: The Psychosocial Risk Index (PRI) is an academic decision-support indicator developed for educational research at SLIIT Kandy. It is not a clinical psychological evaluation or psychiatric diagnosis.
